newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open little changed, eye on data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open little changed, eye on data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in quiet trade on Monday, disregarding weakness in the currency, with the market largely focused on Canadian and economic data due out this week, analysts said.

"There's no data for either Canada or the U.S. The weakness that we see in the Canadian dollar might be dragging on bonds a little bit but not to a significant degree. People are basically in a wait and see mode," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research for ABN AMRO Bank Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$110.75 to yield 7.089 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the two bonds was 20 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.

Among the key economic reports due out this week are the Canadian and U.S. consumer price index reports for April, out on Thursday. Investors will be scouring those and other reports for clues about the timing of the next likely move in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.
"Market expectations are for friendly data this week from the U.S.," said Pyle.
Recent weakness in the Canadian dollar did not weigh heavily on the Canadian bond market this morning, analysts said.

The dollar fell sharply on Friday as investors sold the unit against the Japanese yen. Canada's dollar opened flat this morning at C$1.3917 (US$0.7185) in light trading after being sidelined overnight in an overseas session marked by heavy U.S. dollar-Japanese yen cross-selling, traders said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$103.10 to yield 6.557 percent. The U.S. bond traded unchanged to yield 6.67 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 13 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.04 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.16 percent.
